{{Short description|51st season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1981–82 National Hurling League |image = |dates = 11 October 1981 – 18 April 1982 |teams = |team1 = Kilkenny |captain1 = |manager1 = |titles = 5th |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |two = |three = |four = |previous = [[1980–81 National Hurling League|1980–81]] |next = [[1982–83 National Hurling League|1982–83]] }} The '''1981–82 National Hurling League''' was the 51st season of the [[National Hurling League]]. ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=1981-82 |winners=[[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]
5th National League title
Captain: [[Brian Cody]]
Manager: [[Pat Henderson (hurler)|Pat Henderson]] |relegated= |continentalcup1= |continentalcup1 qualifiers= |continentalcup2= |continentalcup2 qualifiers= |league topscorer= |best goalkeeper= |biggest home win= |biggest away win= |highest scoring= |matches= |total goals= |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |highest attendance= |lowest attendance= |attendance= |average attendance= |prevseason=[[1980-81 National Hurling League|1980-81]] |nextseason=[[1982-83 National Hurling League|1982-83]] |updated=12 March 2017 }} [[Cork GAA|Cork]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[1980-81 National Hurling League|1980-81 season]]. [[Carlow GAA|Carlow]] entered Division 1 as the promoted team. On 18 April 1982, [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] won the title after a 2-14 to 1-11 win over [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the final.
